edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De corona militis, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Serva Deo rem suam intaminatam. Ille eam, si volet, coronabit; imo et vult; denique invitat: Qui vicerit, inquit, dabo ei coronam vitae. Esto et tu fidelis ad mortem. Decerta et tu bonum agonem, cujus coronam et Apostolus repositam sibi merito confidit. Accipit et angelus victoriae coronam procedens in candido equo, ut vinceret. Et alius iridis ambitu ornatur, coelesti prato. Sedent et presbyteri coronati: eodemque auro et ipse Filius hominis supra nubem micat. Si tales imagines in visione, quales veritates in repraesentatione? illas aspice, illas odora. Quid caput strophiolo aut dracontario damnas, diademati destinatum? Nam et reges nos Deo et Patri suo fecit Christus Jesus. Quid tibi cum flore morituro? Habes florem ex virga Jesse, super quem tota divini spiritus gratia requievit, florem incorruptum, immarcescibilem, sempiternum: quem et bonus miles eligendo, in coelesti ordinatione, dignatione profecit. Erubescite, commilitones ejus, jam non ab ipso judicandi, sed ab aliquo Mithrae milite, qui cum initiatur in spelaeo, in castris vere tenebrarum, coronam interposito gladio sibi oblatam, quasi mimum martyrii, dehinc capiti suo accommodatam, monetur obvia manu a capite pellere, et in humerum, si forte, transferre, dicens Mithram esse coronam suam, atque exinde numquam coronatur, idque in signum habet ad probationem sui, sicubi tentatus fuerit de sacramento: statimque creditur Mithrae miles, si dejecerit coronam, si eam in Deo suo esse dixerit. Agnoscamus ingenia diaboli, idcirco quaedam de divinis affectantis, ut nos de suorum fide confundat et judicet.
pass_a_gloss: Keep for God her own thing intact. He, if He will, will crown her; indeed He also wills; finally He invites: He says, To him who conquers, I will give the crown of life. Be also you faithful to death. Contend also you the good contest, whose crown also the Apostle with merit confidently trusts has been laid up for him. The angel also receives the crown of victory, proceeding on a white horse, so that he may conquer. And another is adorned with the circle of the rainbow, with the heavenly meadow. The presbyters also sit crowned: and with the same gold also the Son of Man shines above the cloud. If such images in vision, what truths in representation? Look at those, smell those. Why do you condemn the head with a wreath or a snake-like band, destined for a diadem? For Christ Jesus also made us kings to God and to His Father. What to you with the dying flower? You have the flower from the rod of Jesse, on which the whole grace of the divine Spirit rested, the incorrupt, unwithering, eternal flower: which also the good soldier, by choosing, in the heavenly order, with dignity, advanced. Be ashamed, fellow soldiers of His, now not being judged by Him, but by some soldier of Mithra, who, when he is initiated in the cave, in the camps of true darkness, the crown offered to him with a sword interposed, as a mockery of martyrdom, afterwards accommodated to his head, is warned by a hand presented to him to push it away from his head, and to transfer it to his shoulder, if perhaps, saying Mithra is his crown, and from then on is never crowned, and this he has as a sign for his testing, wherever he may be tested about the sacrament: and immediately the soldier of Mithra is believed, if he throws away the crown, if he says it is in his God: let us recognize the cleverness of the devil, therefore affecting certain things of the divine, so that he may confuse and judge us about the faith of his own.

bible_refs.note: To him who conquers, I will give the crown of life

pass_b_english: Keep what belongs to God intact. He will crown it if He wishes—and He does wish it; in fact, He extends the invitation: "To the one who conquers I will give the crown of life" (Rev 2:10). Be faithful to death yourself. Fight the good contest, the very one whose crown the Apostle confidently trusted had been laid up for him. The angel also receives the crown of victory, riding out on a white horse so that he may conquer. Another is adorned with a rainbow's circle, a heavenly meadow. The presbyters sit crowned, and with that same gold the Son of Man shines above the cloud. If such images appear in a vision, what truths must exist in the reality? Look at them, inhale them. Why do you condemn a head destined for a diadem with a mere wreath or a snake-like band? Christ Jesus has made us kings to God and His Father. What do you want with a flower that dies? You have the flower from the rod of Jesse, the one on whom the full grace of the divine Spirit rested—the incorrupt, unwithering, eternal flower. By choosing it, the good soldier advanced in dignity within the heavenly order. Be ashamed, His fellow-soldiers: you are now being judged not by Him but by some soldier of Mithras. When that initiate enters the cave—in the camps of true darkness—a crown is offered to him with a sword interposed, a mockery of martyrdom, then fitted to his head. He is warned by an outstretched hand to push it from his head and transfer it to his shoulder, if he can, declaring that Mithras is his crown. From then on he is never crowned again; he keeps this as a sign for his testing, so that wherever he is questioned about the sacrament he can prove himself. The Mithraic soldier is believed the moment he throws away the crown and says it belongs to his god. Recognize the devil's cunning: he mimics certain divine realities precisely to confuse us and pass judgment on us through the faith of his own followers.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent translation that preserves all nuances, including the Mithraic ritual description and the theological distinctions. The scripture citation (Rev 2:10) is correctly added to the quote 'To him who conquers, I will give the crown of life' which corresponds to 'Qui vicerit, inquit, dabo ei coronam vitae'.
